Summary: Stratum HyperIndex is a B2B SaaS search provider for regulated verticals (legal + finance). They are moving from an Elastic + custom ANN stack to a dedicated inference+vector serving platform to hit latency and cost targets at 100M+ vectors. Key ask: sub-100ms p99 for reranked top-K on production queries; total cost-per-query target < $0.001 (embeddings + reranker).

Context / constraints:
- Index size target: 300M active vectors, long-term plan 1B+ including cold archives.
- Ingest pattern: continuous stream (Kafka) with heavy daily deltas; want incremental sharding and sparse compaction.
- Query profile: mix of small explorer queries and high-throughput API (avg qps 1200, peak 3k).
- Reranking: two-stage pipeline — ANN recall (GPU pool) -> lightweight transformer reranker (FP16/INT8) for top-40. Reranker must be low-cost and optional fall back to cheaper model.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 30ms, p95 < 60ms, p99 < 100ms for reranked responses.
- Cost sensitivity: internal SKU target to hit OCC <$0.002 per served query, prefer batching & KV-prefix caching.
- Security: must support VPC-private control plane, bring-your-own-KMS, retention controls and full audit trails for queries and model versions.

Quotes from calls: "We can tolerate slightly higher recall latency if unit-cost is predictable — predictable economics matter more than raw lowest latency." — CTO
"Need a plan for cold/hot tiering; we can't keep all 1B vectors hot." — Head of Retrieval

Requirements (extracted):
- Dedicated GPU pools with predictable throughput and autoscale/burst.
- Two-tier routing: hot shards on GPU pods, warm shards on CPU quantized embeddings, automatic fallback.
- Automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated session queries.
- Quantized model support (8-bit/4-bit) with recommended tradeoffs for reranker quality vs cost.
- Ingest: stream friendly APIs + bulk backfill with shard rebalancing.
- Monitoring: token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, regressions alerts tied to eval sets.

Technical notes from SE (Devon):

- Reranker: run on mixed-precision INT8/FP16; keep a CPU cheap fallback (tiny transformer) with auto-fallback policy.
- Ingestion: checkpointed Kafka consumer with snapshotting to avoid replays during rebalance.
